extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection via string-concatenated Jinja template — Arbitrary Jinja expression evaluation, potentially leading to remote code execution via sandbox escape gadgets [verified: fragment is concatenated into the raw Jinja template source (`"Result: " + fragment`) before compilation and rendered with no sandboxing beyond the shared-secret gate, so any caller who knows the internal token can inject `{{ }}` expressions evaluated by the full Jinja engine.]

Path traversal arbitrary file write in dispatch_dock_shelf_498 — Arbitrary file write/overwrite on the server, potentially leading to remote code execution via overwriting application files [verified: name is attacker-controlled and joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no containment check before write_bytes, enabling arbitrary file write.]

Path traversal arbitrary file read in dispatch_cargo_slot_050 — Read arbitrary files on the server filesystem readable by the app process [verified: packet_ref is joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no normalization/containment, allowing ../ traversal to read arbitrary files.]

SSRF via unrestricted url parameter in dispatch_carrier_echo_051 — Attacker can pivot into internal network, reach cloud metadata services (credential theft) or internal-only APIs [verified: url is fully attacker-controlled and passed directly to urlopen with no scheme/host allowlist; gate token doesn't restrict target.]

Sensitive Authorization header written to logs — Credential/token disclosure to anyone with log access, enabling session/account takeover [verified: the raw Authorization header is passed directly to `logger.warning`, persisting bearer tokens in plaintext logs with no redaction.]

Reflected XSS via jinja2 |safe filter — Reflected cross-site scripting allowing script execution in the victim's browser session [verified: the `card` value is rendered via `|safe`, disabling autoescaping, so attacker-supplied HTML/JS in the query param is reflected verbatim into the HTMLResponse.]

XXE via lxml parser with DTD/entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF, or denial of service via crafted XML entities [verified: XMLParser explicitly enables load_dtd and resolve_entities with no_network=False on attacker-controlled body, enabling XXE.]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized Mongo query filter — Bypass intended query logic, extract unintended documents, or trigger $where JavaScript execution depending on MongoDB configuration [verified: filter key from raw JSON body passed unvalidated as MongoDB query document, permitting operator injection.]

Password reset tokens persisted in plaintext outbox log — Any actor with read access to the log file can hijack the password reset flow for any user and take over their account [verified: password_reset_request writes the plaintext valid reset token to storage/mock_outbox/password_resets.log with no access restriction shown; anyone with filesystem access can read it and take over any account.]

Open redirect via unsanitized lane parameter — Phishing via a trusted-domain redirect to attacker-controlled sites [verified: lane parameter used unchanged in RedirectResponse with no same-origin/relative-path allowlist.]

Code injection via eval() of user-supplied expression — Potential arbitrary code execution or sandbox escape from a restricted eval, denial of service via crafted expressions [verified: eval() on attacker-controlled expr string even with stripped builtins remains a code-execution/DoS primitive with no legitimate need for eval.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed requests to this endpoint and read authenticated responses, bypassing same-origin policy [verified: Origin header reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Allow-Credentials: true, permitting any origin credentialed access.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks on the outbound connection, allowing interception/modification of traffic [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() explicitly disables certificate verification for an outbound HTTPS request.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag — Session token can be captured via network interception on any non-HTTPS access path, leading to session hijacking [verified: login() hardcodes secure=False on the session cookie with no env-based toggle, so the auth cookie is sent over plaintext HTTP in any non-HTTPS deployment path.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag — Session hijacking via network interception (MITM) of the auth cookie when the app is served over HTTP [verified: Duplicate of idx1 - same secure=False cookie flag at main.py:269, confirmed same evidence.]

CSV formula injection in exported reports — Formula/DDE injection leads to arbitrary command execution or data exfiltration on the machine of the ops_admin/dispatcher who opens the exported CSV [verified: csv_response() writes DictWriter rows directly from user-controlled fields (title, instructions, internal_notes, company_name, etc.) with no leading-character escaping/quoting, and export() serves these to ops_admin/dispatcher; classic CSV formula injection.]

Security headers explicitly disabled — Removes defense-in-depth browser protections, increasing exploitability of any XSS on this origin [verified: CSP and X-XSS-Protection are explicitly cleared/disabled on this response with no compensating header set elsewhere, removing browser-side mitigations for this route.]

Weak PRNG used for nonce/code generation — Predictable tokens/nonces could be brute-forced or predicted, undermining any security property relying on them [verified: random.choice (non-CSPRNG) used to generate a nonce/code, making it predictable if used for security purposes.]

Internal configuration disclosure via trace/debug endpoint — Discloses internal environment name and filesystem paths, aiding further attacks such as path traversal targeting [verified: the endpoint returns APP_ENV and the internal export base path in the response body, and the only protection is a shared static-token header check (`_wrk_gate`), which is a weak gate rather than real authn/authz.]
